title: spec-gate v1.0: the final release
description:
## Goal

`spec-gate` v1.0, the final release. Every requirement in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` and every decision in `docs/design.md` §10 is implemented and judged by `spec-gate` itself. At least one product other than `spec-gate` has adopted it end to end. A newcomer can discover, install and adopt it from the documentation alone.

## Scope

- **Completes the seed requirements v0 left out:**
  - `sg-ubq` (a local run records nothing);
  - `sg-212` (the agent report);
  - `sg-3zr` (binding check, via `binding-contract`, D-24).
- **Authoritative runner** with commit statuses on a dedicated host (D-16), and write protection of the spec checkout (D-22).
- **Stages:**
  - holdout (D-12, D-13);
  - structure, purity and API/wire, configured on the spec side (design §6);
  - mutation through the specs (D-17).
- **Release and promotion** of judges (D-18).
- **Adoption:**
  - `init` scaffolding for a new product's spec workspace, including aliasing (D-03) and `eventually` (D-05);
  - ratchet mode (D-25);
  - several products in one spec repository (D-21);
  - proof on `req`, after a trivial Rust verification product has been adopted first.
- **Model tier** for spec-gate's own ledger lifecycle (D-10).
- **v0's known limits:** detecting a scenario whose text changed after it was counted.
- **Documentation and discoverability** (cm-155).

## Out of scope

- An LLM judge on correctness.
- Hosting as a multi-tenant service.
- A new BDD framework, mutation tool or prover (design §11).

## Success Criteria

- Every criterion in `spec-gate.req.md` has a scenario, and the ledger holds a red before a green for each one.
- `v1.0` is tagged and promoted by the D-18 path, judged by its predecessor.
- The second product's merges are gated by `spec-gate` commit statuses.
- The documentation is enough for a newcomer to adopt it without help.

## Operator decision

> "accept all" — operator, 2026-10-21, accepting D-01 to D-25 as recorded in `docs/design.md` §10.

> "let's add v1 epic beads for the final release version," — operator, 2026-10-21.

Approves:

- filing this epic;
- implementing D-01 to D-25 as worded, including the edits to `~/code/tools` they name: extending `binding-contract` to read Gherkin tags (D-24), and a `rule-gate` hook (D-22);
- the gates house rules require in the two new repositories.

> "github, req, no Elixir let's create a more trivial rust project for verifications, add beads to block waiting to complete missing features, add epic to complete missing features." — operator, 2026-10-21.

This also approves:

- **Commit statuses on GitHub** (`gate-6l3.1`).
- **`req` as the second adoption product** (`gate-6l3.2`). That includes the edits to `~/code/tools/req` its adoption needs: moving its specs into a spec repository, and branch protection.
- **No Elixir:** the software factory is out of v1.
- **A trivial Rust verification product** with its own spec repository (`gate-6l3.31`, `gate-6l3.32`). It is the first external product judged by `spec-gate`, and the documentation's worked example.
- **v1.0 waits for `binding-contract`** (`gate-6l3.4`). The binding stage is blocked by `gate-6l3.30`, which waits on `tools-trace-audit-landing-hmq` in `~/code/tools/.beads`.

> "accept all" — operator, 2026-10-21, accepting the recommendations for gate-6l3.3, gate-6l3.33, and the four defaults (gate-c7r.7, gate-6l3.31, gate-6l3.12, gate-6l3.26).

This approves:

- The text-change rule (`gate-6l3.3`, recorded in `gate-6l3.24`).
- Public product and spec repositories, with a private holdout repository (`gate-6l3.33`).
- The four defaults:
  - permanent rejection under an id;
  - `basket` over HTTP;
  - a collaborator account for agents, with no-bypass branch protection;
  - `hegeltest` stateful testing for the model tier.

Nothing else is approved. Every new policy question goes to a `decision` bead, and the beads that depend on it stay blocked until the operator answers there.

title: Decide where commit statuses live
description:
## Question

Where do commit statuses live? The runner (D-16) posts a status that branch protection requires, but neither repository has a remote.

## Options

- (a) GitHub remotes, with statuses through the GitHub API.
- (b) A self-hosted forge on the homelab (Forgejo or Gitea), with statuses through its API.
- (c) No forge. A status file in the spec repository, and a local pre-merge hook that reads it.

## Blocks

The runner spec and implementation, runner provisioning, the second-product adoption proof.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The operator's answer is quoted verbatim with its date in this bead's notes, and the blocked beads are updated to match.

title: Specify the authoritative runner and commit statuses
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in the v1 epic)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Its invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement, meaning the specs, the drivers, the ledger, the judge pin and the verdict. There are two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate` is the product. Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs` is its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). An agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

Design and the 25 recorded decisions are in `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements live in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md`, with ids minted by `~/code/tools/req` and never written by hand. House rules are in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

**Dog-fooding from v0 on.**

- Every product commit is judged by the pinned judge in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml`. Before the runner exists (`side:infra`), the operator runs the judgment by hand; after that, the runner does.
- A spec bead is done when its scenarios are merged and the judge has recorded each one red against the current product commit.
- A product bead is done when the judge's verdict for its commit is pass and each scenario it targets has a red before its green in the ledger.
- A bead that adds a judging capability ends with a release `v0.N` promoted per D-18. Each later bead is then judged by a judge that already has that capability.

**Tests, per house rules:**

- acceptance as Gherkin in the spec repository (cm-ltj);
- properties with `hegeltest` on entities (cm-eqj);
- unit tests against fake adapters at the ports, run with nextest (cm-wah);
- only a few boundary integration tests (cm-33k);
- the zero, one and many cases (cm-srn);
- no loops in tests (cm-o9o);
- `cargo mutants`, with survivors triaged through `mutation-triage`, before closing (cm-1qk).

Every gate added must be seen red once on a planted violation (cm-yzv).

## What

Requirements and scenarios for the authoritative runner (D-16):
- A product push triggers a judgment of that commit against spec `main`.
- Exactly one commit status is posted per judgment, naming the product commit, the spec commit and the judge.
- The status credential is held only by the runner's OS user.
- A judgment that cannot complete posts a void status, never a pass.
- A second push while a judgment is running does not corrupt the ledger.

Statuses live on GitHub (`gate-6l3.1`). They must satisfy these properties:

- The required status check is satisfied only by a status from the runner's GitHub App, so a status posted with any other credential does not count.
- The runner polls GitHub instead of receiving webhooks, so nothing on the homelab is exposed to the internet.
- The agents' GitHub credentials can push branches and open pull requests, but carry no Administration or Statuses permission. Without that, an agent could post its own status or switch protection off.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The requirements are minted with `req`, and every criterion has one scenario.
- Each requirement has a witness and a near-miss (`~/kbe/guides/writing-specifications.md`).
- The judge has recorded each scenario red against the current product.
- Delivered as a branch for operator merge.

- The status credential is readable only by that user.

- A push to `spec-gate` produces a status, naming both commits, without operator action.
- An agent session on its usual host cannot read the credential. Verify by attempting the read from that host.
- A merge without a passing status is refused.
- A status posted with the agent's credential does not satisfy the required check. Verify by trying.
- The agent's credential cannot change branch protection. Verify by trying.

title: spec-gate v0: the first trusted judge
description:
## Goal

`spec-gate` v0: the first trusted judge. It runs `spec-gate-specs` against a `spec-gate` commit and refuses a scenario that was never seen red. It fails a run on skipped or undefined steps, and on zero scenarios. It mints scenario ids. It refuses to run when its own checksum differs from the pin. Everything else in `docs/design.md` is out of v0.

## In scope (criteria in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md`)

- `sg-dop.1`, `sg-dop.2`: the verdict names the product and spec commits, and the spec version is chosen by the spec repository.
- `sg-397.1`–`.3`: red-first.
- `sg-zf8.1`, `sg-zf8.2`: an undefined step or zero scenarios fails the run.
- `sg-i86.1`: checksum refusal.
- The scenario-id minting criteria drafted in `gate-c7r.1`.

## Out of scope

- `sg-3zr.*`: the binding check, owned by `binding-contract` (D-24).
- `sg-ubq.*`: local vs authoritative runs, which need the runner (D-16).
- `sg-212.1`: the full agent report.
- The holdout, mutation-through-specs, structure, purity and contract stages; the runner host; commit statuses; the `rule-gate` write block (D-22). In v0, the separation between the spec and product repositories is held by operator review alone.

## How the bootstrap works

1. The product scaffold commit builds a stub binary that implements no behaviour. It is the red baseline: every in-scope scenario fails against it for its stated reason.
2. v0 is built and reviewed, tagged `v0`, and its checksum is pinned.
3. Pinned v0 mints `@id` tags into `spec-gate-specs` (reviewed and merged by the operator).
4. Pinned v0 judges the scaffold commit, which records the reds in the ledger.
5. Pinned v0 judges the `v0` commit, which records the greens.

The only self-judgment is step 5. D-19 accepts it: v0 is trusted on review. From the next release on, a judge is always certified by its predecessor (D-18).

## Known limits of v0

- A scenario whose first recorded result is a pass stays rejected under its id. The way out is to remove the `@id` tag and re-mint, which gives a new identity (see `gate-c7r.7`).
- A scenario whose text changes after it was counted keeps its red-first evidence. Nothing in v0 detects that the meaning changed.
- No timeout bounds the product build or the harness run (C-35). The operator kills a stuck run.
- Only plain `Scenario:` blocks are accepted; Outlines, `Background:` and `Rule:` are refused (C-13, C-22, C-28).

## Success Criteria

- Every in-scope scenario has a ledger red against the scaffold commit, and a later green against the `v0` commit.
- The acceptance harness was seen failing on a deliberately undefined step.
- The operator has reviewed v0, signed tag `v0`, and pinned its sha256 in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml`.
- The ledger and the `@id` tags are merged to `spec-gate-specs` `main`.

## Operator decision

> "accept all" — operator, 2026-10-21, accepting the recommendations for D-01 to D-25 as recorded in `docs/design.md` §10.

> "commit both and file the v0 epic" — operator, 2026-10-21.

> "find a way to make it work" — operator, 2026-10-21, in reply to the two flagged assumptions: whether mint is in v0, and how seed reds are recorded before v0 exists.

> "push mutation-triage to origin, accept all" — operator, 2026-10-22, accepting the recommendations of the clarify pass recorded under "## Clarify answers" (C-1 to C-17).

> "accept all" — operator, 2026-10-22, accepting the recommendations of the second clarify pass (C-18 to C-27) and the rewrite of the stale bead descriptions.

> "accept all, merge the readme branch, push, run one more pass, what you recommended." — operator, 2026-10-22, accepting the third clarify pass (C-28 to C-35).

Approves:

- The 25 decisions as worded in `docs/design.md` §10.
- Filing this epic.
- `spec-gate mint` as part of v0. Red-first keys its ledger on minted ids (D-20), and ids are never written by hand, so v0 has no red-first without mint.

The contract between the three parties to a judgment: the judging `spec-gate`, the spec repository's acceptance harness, and the product. - **The ledger format.** Append-only, one entry per scenario per judgment, keyed by scenario `@id`, product commit and spec commit. It is diffable in git.
- **`spec-gate.toml`.**
  - `[sut]`: how the product is checked out and built.
  - `[judge]`: the pin.
  - `[gates] acceptance`: the harness is a command plus a results file, so a fixture spec repository can supply a trivial command that prints canned results instead of a Rust crate to build.
- **The harness results format** that `spec-gate` reads: per scenario, its tags, its result, and each step's result, including skipped and undefined. Prefer a format `cucumber` 0.23 already writes (its `output-json` feature) over a new one.

description:

## What

The entities of red-first, as a pure functional core (cm-rlh), with no I/O.

- **The scenario lifecycle**, derived from a scenario's ledger entries in order. It is a state machine (cm-prk):
  - a sum type of states, each carrying only the data valid in it;
  - a pure transition function `(state, event) -> (state, effects)`;
  - an exhaustive match with no wildcard.
  
  States must distinguish at least: never seen; seen red (with the first red's product commit); counted; and rejected (its first result was a pass).
- **The verdict function.** It takes the scenario results of one judgment plus each scenario's lifecycle and returns pass, fail or void, with a reason per scenario. Zero scenarios fails (`sg-zf8.2`). Any skipped or undefined step fails, whatever the harness configuration said (`sg-zf8.1`). Any scenario that is not counted fails, named (`sg-397.2`, `.3`). A scenario without an `@id` fails, named (the criterion drafted in `gate-c7r.1`).

**Confirmed by the operator (2026-10-21, "accept all"):** "rejected" is permanent for that id. A later red does not rescue it, because `sg-397.1` requires the red before the first pass. Re-identification (remove the `@id` and re-mint) is the way out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Property tests with `hegeltest` (cm-eqj) over generated ledger-entry sequences prove:
  - a scenario is counted if and only if a red (C-2) precedes its first pass, at a product commit different from that first pass (C-7);
  - the transition function is total over every state and event pair;
  - the verdict is pass if and only if at least one scenario ran, every scenario run is counted, no step was skipped or undefined, and every scenario run passed in this judgment (C-6).
- The zero, one and many cases (cm-srn) are each an explicit example test: no entries; one red; red then green; green first; many scenarios with mixed results.
- `effect-audit` passes on the core crate.
- `cargo mutants` on the changed code, with survivors triaged through `mutation-triage` (cm-1qk). Every survivor is either killed or recorded as equivalent.

## Clarify answers

Binding on this bead; approved by the operator on 2026-10-22 (epic `gate-c7r`, "## Operator decision"). The full list is in the epic.

- **C-2** A red is a judgment in which the scenario's first non-passing step has status `failed` and is a `Then`, or an `And`/`But` that follows a `Then`. A `failed` `Given` or `When`, and an `undefined`, `ambiguous` or `skipped` step, are recorded as broken and give no red-first evidence.
- **C-6** The verdict is pass if and only if there is at least one scenario run, every scenario run is counted, no step was skipped or undefined, and every scenario run passed in this judgment.
- **C-7** Red-first evidence needs a red at a product commit different from the scenario's first green. Judging the same (product, spec) pair again is allowed and appends.
- **C-21** Two scenarios sharing an `@id`, a scenario with more than one `@id`, or an `@id` that does not parse as a hashid with the `[mint] prefix`: the judge fails, naming every scenario involved, and `mint` refuses, naming them and changing no file. An `@id` that does not parse counts as missing. `.1` drafts these criteria.
- **C-30** A judgment that fails under C-21 appends an entry for every scenario with exactly one valid `@id` that no other scenario shares, and nothing for the scenarios C-21 involves.

  - `clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm` at deny (cm-prk);
  - a no-comments gate that fails on any code comment except toolchain directives (cm-k7c);
  - `cargo nextest run`.
  
  One command runs them all.
- **The stub** exposes the CLI surface from `gate-c7r.5` and implements no behaviour. Every command exits with a not-implemented error that is distinct from every outcome in the contract. It must never emulate a verdict: a stub that always exits "fail" would turn every "the verdict is fail" scenario green before any red was seen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo build --release --locked` succeeds.
- The gate command passes, and each gate was seen red once on a planted violation: a forbidden crate edge, an effect in a domain crate, a wildcard arm on an enum, and a comment.
- Every command of the stub exits with the not-implemented status, covered by one integration test per command.
- The close note records the scaffold commit SHA.

## Clarify answers

Binding on this bead; approved by the operator on 2026-10-22 (epic `gate-c7r`, "## Operator decision"). The full list is in the epic.

- **C-5** The contract reserves the stub's not-implemented exit status. The CLI driver maps it to a typed outcome, so the `Then` is what fails; any other unrecognised status is a `DriverError`.
- **C-16** The `docs/design.md` §6 and §7 update moves from `.5` to `.8`: a spec-side bead does not write to the product repository (D-11).
- **C-17** The no-comments gate (cm-k7c) is the new tool `~/code/tools/no-comments`. `.2` and `.8` wait on it through `gate-c7r.12`.

title: spec-gate mint
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The `spec-gate mint` use case, satisfying the minting criteria drafted in `gate-c7r.1`. It edits the feature files in place:
- adds an `@id` tag to every scenario that lacks one;
- never overwrites an existing id;
- never reuses an id;
- decides uniqueness against every `features/**/*.feature` file (C-23) plus every id in `ledger/` (C-3).

Ids are minted with the `hashid` crate, a git dependency on `github.com/igouss/hashid` pinned to `7d6def2` (C-15), seeded deterministically (C-20).

"Never re-mint" is an invariant to make unrepresentable rather than check (cm-jiu): the mint operation accepts only a scenario that carries no id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Properties (`hegeltest`) prove:
  - running mint twice gives the same files as running it once;
  - no existing id changes;
  - every id across the repository is unique after mint.
- Unit tests against a fake feature-file port (cm-wah) cover zero, one and many untagged scenarios, and many files.
- One boundary integration test on real files in a temporary directory (cm-33k).
- `cargo mutants` on the changed code, with survivors triaged.
- The minting scenarios from `gate-c7r.1` pass when the harness runs against this commit.

## Clarify answers

Binding on this bead; approved by the operator on 2026-10-22 (epic `gate-c7r`, "## Operator decision"). The full list is in the epic.

- **C-3** `mint` decides uniqueness against the live `@id` tags in every feature file plus every id in `ledger/`. Flagged assumption: an id minted and deleted before any judgment could be reused.
- **C-4** The scenario-id prefix is `[mint] prefix` in `spec-gate.toml`; this repository uses `sgs`, distinct from the criterion prefix `sg`.
- **C-12** Only `judge` checks the checksum against the pin; `mint` does not. Mint's diff is protected by the operator's merge review.
- **C-13** v0 refuses Scenario Outlines in `mint` and `judge`, naming the outline.
- **C-15** `hashid` is a git dependency on `github.com/igouss/hashid` pinned to `7d6def2` (on `origin/main`, checked 2026-10-22).
- **C-20** `mint` seeds `hashid` deterministically: the title is the feature file path plus the scenario name, and the creation time is a fixed constant, never the clock. Re-adding a deleted scenario under its old name therefore collides with its id in `ledger/`, so the "never reuses an id" scenario can be written as a black-box near-miss. No clock input is added (D-05).
- **C-21** Two scenarios sharing an `@id`, a scenario with more than one `@id`, or an `@id` that does not parse as a hashid with the `[mint] prefix`: the judge fails, naming every scenario involved, and `mint` refuses, naming them and changing no file. An `@id` that does not parse counts as missing. `.1` drafts these criteria.
- **C-22** The Scenario Outline refusal (C-13) is a void judgment naming the outline, with nothing appended. `mint` exits with a non-success status, names the outline, and changes no file. Neither uses the refused status, which belongs to the checksum (`sg-i86.1`).
- **C-23** "Every feature file" means `features/**/*.feature` in the spec repository, for `mint` and for the judge. Fixtures keep no `.feature` files there.
- **C-24** `mint` has its own success exit status in the contract, distinct from the stub's not-implemented status (C-5), and every mint scenario's `Then` asserts it, so no mint scenario passes against the do-nothing scaffold.
- **C-28** v0 accepts only plain `Scenario:` blocks. A `Background:`, a `Rule:`, an `@id` or `@covers:` tag on a `Feature:` or `Rule:` line, or a file under `features/**` that does not parse makes the judgment void, naming the file and the construct, with nothing appended; `mint` exits with a non-success status, names them, and changes no file. Neither uses the refused status.
- **C-32** `mint` changes no byte of a feature file except inserting `@id` tag text. `.1` drafts this as a criterion; `.9` proves it as a property (output equals input with only tag text inserted).
- **C-33** `mint` takes no argument that narrows which scenarios it tags in v0: it always tags every untagged scenario under `features/**/*.feature`.
- **C-34** `mint` passes `hashid` a population of 0, no description and no creator; the title's path is relative to the spec repository root with `/` separators. Every input is fixed, so the C-20 collision holds at any repository size; `hashid`'s escalation handles further collisions. C-20 and C-34 override the timestamp seed described in `req`'s IDS section for `spec-gate mint`.
